home.faq.q1: How do I know the final price?
home.faq.a1: Online notarization and company formation have fixed prices that you see before paying; state and government fees are shown on a separate line. For translations, apostilles, tax returns and other documents, we take a quick look first and send a written quote. You pay only once you agree to it.
home.faq.q2: Do you give legal advice or go to court?
home.faq.a2: No. VitaCoreX is not a law firm. We prepare and organize documents at your direction and take care of the paperwork. If you need a lawyer, we can pass a short summary to an independent attorney, only with your consent.
home.faq.q3: Which languages do you work in?
home.faq.a3: We work with clients in English, Russian and Spanish. For translations, send any language pair: our coordinator checks which qualified translator can take it and gives you the price and date before you order.
home.faq.a4: That's always up to the office receiving it. Florida online notarizations and certified translations are common practice, but check the recipient's requirements first. We'll tell you what to ask.
home.faq.q5: How do I send documents safely?
home.faq.a5: Not through the website form, and not by email. Once we've agreed on the work, we send you a private upload link. Never send Social Security numbers, bank details or ID scans by email or through a form.
home.faq.a6: Yes. Most services are online, across the U.S. For company formation and apostilles, it depends on the state involved. Small-claims work for companies depends on the state and court, and we don't take business cases in New York.

ap.title: Apostilles for U.S. documents going abroad
ap.lead: Tell us where the document was issued and which country needs it. We find the office that issues the apostille, prepare the request and track it, with every cost listed before you pay.
ap.route.title: Where it goes depends on who issued the document
ap.route.lead: There's no single apostille office for every document. We work this out before we send a quote.
ap.route.state.d: Birth and marriage certificates, court records, notarized documents. Usually the Secretary of State of the state that issued or notarized the document.
ap.route.fed.d: For example FBI background checks or other federal records. These go to the U.S. Department of State, not to a state office.
ap.route.foreign.d: An apostille can only be issued in the country where the document was issued. We explain the options and what can be done in the U.S., such as a certified translation.
ap.faq.q1: Does every country accept an apostille?
ap.faq.a1: Only countries that are party to the Hague Apostille Convention. For other countries a different process (legalization through an embassy) applies; we tell you which one fits.
ap.faq.a2: Usually an original or a certified copy issued by the official office is required. A plain photocopy is generally not enough. We confirm the requirement for your document.
ap.faq.a3: It depends on the issuing office and shipping. We give you an estimate with the quote and update you at each step.

ron.title: Notarize your document online
ron.lead: A live video session with a Florida Notary Public. You need a valid government photo ID, a device with a camera and the unsigned document.
ron.how.title: From booking to a notarized document
ron.how.s1.d: Document type, where you will be, and whether you have a valid photo ID. The fee for one notarial act is paid on a secure payment page.
ron.how.s2.d: Pick a slot in our calendar. Your appointment is confirmed once the calendar's confirmation email arrives.
ron.how.s3.d: The platform checks your identity, you sign, and the notary completes the electronic notarization. You receive the notarized document electronically.
ron.req.title: What you need
ron.req.1: A valid, unexpired government photo ID for every signer
ron.req.2: A computer or phone with a camera, microphone and stable internet
ron.req.3: The complete document, not yet signed
ron.req.4: Every signer present on the video call
ron.limits.title: Good to know
ron.limits.1: You choose the type of notarial act. The notary cannot choose it for you or advise on the content of your document.
ron.limits.2: The office that receives your document decides what it accepts. For use abroad you may also need an apostille.
ron.limits.3: Signing from outside the United States? Say so in your request, and we'll first check whether the notarization is possible.
ron.limits.4: Businesses with many documents: ask for volume pricing.
ron.faq.a1: Steven Miller, founder of VitaCoreX, a Florida Notary Public authorized to perform online notarizations.
ron.faq.a2: The listed price covers one notarial act. Additional signatures or acts, witnesses and a mailed paper copy are separate and shown before you pay.
ron.faq.q3: Will an office in another state accept it?
ron.faq.a3: Most U.S. offices accept notarizations by a notary of another state, but the receiving office decides. Check its requirements before booking.
ron.faq.q4: What if I cancel or the session cannot go ahead?
ron.faq.a4: Contact us before the appointment to reschedule. If we cannot complete the notarization, we tell you why and what your options are.

tr.title: Translations for any language pair
tr.lead: Certified translations for USCIS, courts, schools and banks, plus general translations of letters and business texts. We confirm the translator, the price and the date before you pay.
tr.est.title: How much will my translation cost?
tr.est.lead: Prices are counted in words of the original. A standard page is 250 words; a typical birth certificate fits on one page. This is a guide, not the final price: we confirm it once we see the document.
tr.est.words: Number of words in the original
tr.opt.title: Certified or general?
tr.opt.lead: Choose certified if the document goes to an agency, court, school or bank. A general translation is enough for letters, websites and texts for your own use.
tr.team.title: The right translator for each language pair
tr.team.lead: Polina Zaic, our linguist and translation coordinator, translates in her own language pairs and assigns qualified translators for other languages. Before you pay, we tell you who can take your pair and when the work will be ready.
tr.faq.q1: Does USCIS need a notarized translation?
tr.faq.a1: No. USCIS asks for a complete English translation and a translator's certification that the translation is accurate and that the translator is competent. Notarization is an optional extra some other offices ask for.
tr.faq.q2: How do I send the document?
tr.faq.a2: After you accept the quote, we send a private upload link. Please do not attach documents to the request form or to email.
tr.faq.a3: Send any language pair. We confirm whether a qualified translator is available, the price and the date before you order. Rare languages may cost more.
tr.faq.q4: Can I get a printed copy?
tr.faq.a4: Yes. Printed copies and postage are quoted separately, line by line, before you pay.

nc.meta.desc: Florida court name change: your petition packet prepared from your answers, county filing instructions and a full cost estimate. Fixed service fee; court and background-check fees listed separately.
nc.title: Change your name through a Florida court
nc.lead: We prepare your petition packet from your answers and write out how to file it in your county. Our fee is fixed; the court's fees are listed separately below, so you see the whole cost before you start.
nc.aside.family: For a child or a whole family:
nc.extra.title: Paid separately
nc.cost.title: The whole cost, line by line
nc.cost.lead: Pick your county. Our fee stays the same; court and background-check fees are paid by you directly to the clerk and to the state.
nc.cost.src: Fees as published by county clerks, checked in October 2026. The clerk's fee on the day you file is the one that applies.
nc.est.caption: Estimated cost of a Florida court name change
nc.est.paynote: You pay VitaCoreX {ours}. The rest, {rest}, goes directly to the court, the state and the fingerprint provider.
nc.how.title: How it goes
nc.how.s1.d: Florida requires us to give you a written nonlawyer disclosure first. Then you answer the questions in writing, in English, Russian or Spanish.
nc.how.s2.d: We type the court-approved forms from your answers and add written filing steps for your county.
nc.how.s3.d: You sign and file with the clerk, pay the court fee and complete the background check.
nc.how.s4.d: The court reviews the petition, usually at a short hearing. After the judgment, our checklist shows where to update your name.
nc.family.title: For a child or a whole family
nc.family.lead: A child's name change usually needs the other parent's consent or formal notice, and a family petition covers several people. We look at your situation first and confirm the price in writing.
nc.faq.q1: Will I have to go to court?
nc.faq.a1: Usually there is a short final hearing in front of a judge. The clerk tells you the date and whether it is in person or by video.
nc.faq.q2: If you were born outside Florida or outside the U.S.
nc.faq.a2: That's fine. You can still file in the Florida county where you live. If your birth certificate is not in English, the court may ask for a certified translation, which we can prepare.
nc.faq.q3: Restoring a former name after a divorce
nc.faq.a3: If your divorce case is still open, the name can often be restored in that case. If it is closed, a separate petition works, and fingerprints are usually not needed to restore a former name.
nc.faq.q4: Can you tell me whether I qualify or what to write?
nc.faq.a4: No. We are not a law firm and can't give legal advice. We prepare the approved forms from your own answers. For legal advice, contact an attorney or The Florida Bar Lawyer Referral Service.
nc.strip.title: Ready to change your name?
nc.strip.text: One fixed fee for the packet and the instructions. Court fees go to the clerk and are shown above.
fw.meta.title: Court and USCIS Fee Waiver Applications | VitaCoreX
fw.meta.desc: Court and USCIS fee waiver forms typed from your written answers: Florida civil indigent status, USCIS I-912, federal in forma pauperis and other states. One fixed price per application; the court or USCIS decides.
fw.title: Can't afford the filing fee? Ask to have it waived.
fw.lead: Courts and USCIS can waive or reduce their fees for people with low income. We type the waiver form from your written answers and list the documents it asks for. One price per application, whichever form it is.
fw.which.title: Which waiver do you need?
fw.which.lead: Each court system has its own form. Tell us where your case is or which USCIS form you're filing.
fw.v.fl.d: Application for civil indigent status, filed with the clerk. Used for court fees in cases such as a name change.
fw.v.uscis.d: Request for a fee waiver on eligible immigration forms, filed together with that form. The I-912 itself has no USCIS fee.
fw.v.fed.d: Application to proceed without prepaying fees (AO 240 or AO 239). The judge decides.
fw.v.other.d: Most state courts have a similar form. Tell us the state and the court, and we'll confirm we can prepare it before you pay.
fw.not.title: What we don't do
fw.faq.q1: Can you tell me if I qualify?
fw.faq.a1: No. Only the court or USCIS decides, and we can't advise you on which basis to claim. We type the form exactly from your written answers.
fw.faq.q2: What if the waiver is denied?
fw.faq.a2: You can usually still pay the fee and continue, or follow the instructions in the denial. Our fee covers preparing the application, not the decision.
fw.faq.q3: Why is my name on the form as the preparer?
fw.faq.a3: Many waiver forms, including the I-912, require anyone who helped to sign the preparer section. It shows who typed the form; it does not make us your representative.
fw.faq.q4: Can I get the waiver form for a name change too?
fw.faq.a4: Yes. If you are changing your name through a Florida court and can't afford the court fee, the civil indigent application is a separate application at the same fixed price.
fw.strip.title: One form, one fixed price
fw.strip.text: The same price for every waiver form. The court or USCIS makes the decision.

bf.meta.title: Florida Annual Report, DBA and Company Filings | VitaCoreX
bf.meta.desc: Florida annual report filing for a flat fee plus the state fee, DBA registration, amendments, certificates of status and certified copies. Fixed prices, no automatic renewal.
bf.title: Keep your company active, without the paperwork
bf.lead: Annual reports, trade names, amendments and certificates for Florida companies. We check your Sunbiz record, type the filing and send you the result. State fees are paid at cost.
bf.dl.title: The annual report is due by May 1
bf.dl.text: Florida opens the annual report on January 1. After May 1 the state adds a $400 late fee for LLCs and corporations. That fee goes to the state, not to us. If the report is still not filed, the state can dissolve the company.
bf.self: You can always file it yourself at sunbiz.org and pay only the state fee. VitaCoreX is a private company, not the State of Florida. Our fee pays for checking, typing and tracking the filing.
bf.opt.title: Company filings with fixed prices
bf.opt.lead: One price for our work, plus the state fee at cost. Filings outside Florida are quoted first.
bf.fee.title: What the State of Florida charges
bf.fee.lead: These fees are set by the state and paid to it. We add nothing to them.
bf.fee.caption: Florida Division of Corporations fees, checked October 15, 2026
bf.fee.source: Source: Florida Division of Corporations fee schedule. A DBA also needs a newspaper notice in your county, at the newspaper’s price.
bf.faq.q1: Is this the official state website?
bf.faq.a1: No. VitaCoreX is a private document preparation company. The official site is sunbiz.org, where you can file yourself and pay only the state fee.
bf.faq.q2: What if I already missed May 1?
bf.faq.a2: We can still file. The state adds its $400 late fee, and we show you the total before you pay. If the company was already dissolved, reinstatement is a separate quote.
bf.faq.q3: Does the yearly plan renew automatically?
bf.faq.a3: No. You pay for one year at a time. Before the next year we ask you, and nothing is charged unless you agree.
bf.faq.q4: Do I need a newspaper notice for a DBA?
bf.faq.a4: Yes. Florida law requires the name to be advertised once in a newspaper in the county of your main place of business before you register. We tell you how, or arrange it at the newspaper’s price.
bf.faq.q5: Can you change the owners or members of my company?
bf.faq.a5: We type the changes you have already decided into the state forms. Ownership agreements and their consequences are legal questions; for those we can pass a short summary to an independent attorney, only with your consent.
bf.strip.title: Due this year? Send the company name.
bf.strip.text: We check the Sunbiz record and confirm the state fee before you pay.
